evals.prompt: tldr of where we are? I only want to unblock you.
assertions: Runs git status and checks the current branch and unpushed commits before writing the summary
Answers with exactly four sections in this order: Done, Still to do, What you need to know, Decisions for you
Every branch, commit or pull request it names is a markdown link built from the git remote, or it says the link could not be built
Ends with a single line giving the shortest reply that unblocks the agent

evals.prompt: I'm stepping away for an hour. What do you need me to decide before I go?
assertions: Each decision is numbered and has two or three options, a recommendation with a one-line reason, and what the agent will do once answered
Merging, releasing, deploying or spending money that the session wants to do appears as a decision, not as work the agent will just do
States anything it could not check as unverified instead of reporting it from memory

evals.prompt: Waar staan we nu met deze sessie? Wat moet ik beslissen?
assertions: Answers in Dutch with the four sections
Lists state left behind (uncommitted files, unpushed branches, worktrees) under what the person needs to know, or says there is none

evals.prompt: tldr for PR 42 only, I'll deal with the rest later
assertions: Keeps the four sections but reports only what concerns PR 42
Checks PR 42's current state and CI result before writing instead of restating it from earlier in the conversation
Lists merging PR 42 as a decision for the person, not as a task the agent will do

evals.prompt: Give me a tldr of this article: https://example.com/blog/why-we-moved-to-postgres
assertions: Summarizes the article and does not produce the session sections

evals.prompt: Give me a quick summary of what this repository does and how it is structured.
assertions: Describes the repository's purpose and layout and does not produce the Done / Still to do / Decisions sections
